section.sectionSummaryBrief: The arousal of the singular level of the soul above division must be drawn down gradually into the soul's level of division, reflected in the progression from the unity of "all of you" to the detailed listing of the ten types in the Torah portion.
section.t: Now, the arousal of the aspect of the singular [level] in the soul, which is above division, must be drawn down in a gradual manner into the soul that is in the aspect of division.
[And this is analogous to how this arousal must be connected to physical action,
as in the action of sitting in the sukkah,
taking the Four Species,
and dancing with the feet].
For this is what [happens] after it is stated, "You are standing... all of you...," that all of Israel are in the manner of "all of you"
by virtue of the singular aspect within them,
[the verse] then enumerates all ten types in detail,
from "your heads, your tribes" to "your woodcutters and your water drawers,"
meaning that the concept of "all of you"
(the singular aspect)
of Israel must be evident in them even as they are in the aspect of division.
And just as it is in the soul, so too is it in the year,
that the aspect of the "one day" of Yom Kippur and of Simchas Torah activates and permeates all the days of the year
(beginning from Isru Chag),
so that in all his particular actions
(in all your deeds and in all your ways),
it is evident that he has just come from the "one day" of Yom Kippur and Simchas Torah.
And this matter continues throughout the entire year,
for even though many days, weeks, and months have already passed since Yom Kippur and Simchas Torah,
nevertheless, the arousal of the "one day" is not weakened at all, but stands in its full strength,
since it comes from an aspect that is above the matter of division and change,
the aspect of "I"
—Hashem, I have not changed.
And through the aspect of the "one day," which is above division, being drawn into all the days of the year, which are in the aspect of division and change,
thereby an elevation is also brought about in the aspect of the "one day" itself,
in the manner explained above regarding the matter of the "fruit of the beautiful tree" (esrog), which not only withstands all changes in weather but actually grows from them.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: May it be His will that all the above be fulfilled for every single Jew, granting a good and blessed year in revealed goodness, with children, life, and sustenance both physical and spiritual, permeating all daily affairs with the essential point of the soul.
section.t: And may it be His will,
that all the above be fulfilled for each and every one within the entirety of the Jewish people,
that there be a good and blessed year, with goodness that is seen and revealed below ten handbreadths,
in children, life, and sustenance, and in all of them—prosperity,
both in children, life, and sustenance in their simple sense, and in children, life, and sustenance in the spiritual sense
(from which the matters in their simple sense are drawn down),
that out of joy and goodness of heart, immediately after Simchas Torah, the service of "and Yaakov went on his way"
shall also apply to matters of the permitted [mundane],
[for the matter of "and Yaakov went on his way" that follows Yom Kippur
is in "his way" regarding matters of mitzvos,
since during the four days between Yom Kippur and Sukkos all Israel are occupied with mitzvos.
However, the matter of "and Yaakov went on his way" that follows Simchas Torah is in "his way" also regarding matters of the permitted],
so that on each and every day,
both on weekdays and all the more so on Shabbos and Yom Tov
(including also Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur),
all his affairs are permeated,
both the general matters and the particular matters,
with the essential and innermost point of the innermost aspect and essence of the soul,
which is connected to the innermost aspect and essence of the Ein Sof, blessed be He.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Since this comes from Simchas Torah, whose joy breaks all boundaries, it breaks and nullifies all limitations of exile, leading to the true and complete redemption through Moshiach speedily.
section.t: And since this comes from Simchas Torah,
for joy breaks through all boundaries,
above measure and limitation,
therefore it breaks and nullifies all the boundaries and limitations of the internal exile,
and likewise the boundaries and limitations of exile in its simple sense,
and we merit that very soon, "May our eyes behold Your return to Zion with mercy,"
with the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
may he come and lead us upright to our land, speedily in our actual days,
and may [the Holy Temple] be built,
the Holy Temple in its place, and may He gather the dispersed of Israel, etc.
(and until [the point that])
"Then"
"I will transform the peoples to a pure language... to serve Him"
with one accord,
"and"
"the kingship shall be Hashem's."
